In the exploit:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"javascript\",\n  \"function\": \"function(){java.lang.Runtime.getRuntime().exec('malicious_command');}\",\n  \"\": {\n    \"enabled\": true\n  }\n}\n```\n\nThe empty string `\"\"` as a key would be trying to map to one of the parameters. Jackson has a feature where it can map empty strings to properties that have `@JsonProperty` annotations, or it could be mapped to a property without a name annotation.\n\nActually, wait. Looking more carefully, I think the vulnerability is that the empty string `\"\"` is being mapped to the `dimension` field. Jackson will map an empty string to the `dimension` parameter, which then passes the `dimension != null` check (since an empty string is not null).\n\nThen, when the filter is used, the `getPredicateFactory()` method is called, which checks `config.isEnabled()`.
